reason: The lower-bound construction defeats N=10, while the maximal-sublist argument proves that N=11 always succeeds.
text:
The smallest value is \(\boxed{11}\).

For necessity, let the first player write four copies of \(24\) and five copies of \(23\). Their total is
\[
4\cdot24+5\cdot23=211.
\]
Every proper sublist has sum at most \(211-23=188\), while the whole list has sum \(211\). Thus no selectable sum lies in \([190,210]\), so \(N=10\), and hence every \(N\le 10\), fails.

For sufficiency, consider any permitted list. Suppose no sublist has sum in \([189,211]\). Choose a sublist \(B\) whose sum \(s\le188\) is maximal. Since the total sum is at least \(200\), some term \(x\) is outside \(B\). Maximality gives \(s+x>188\), and the assumed gap then gives \(s+x\ge212\). Since \(x\le25\), we obtain \(s\ge187\). Hence \(s\in\{187,188\}\).

If \(s=187\), every outside term must equal \(25\). Fix such a term. Replacing any \(y\in B\) by this \(25\) gives sum \(212-y\). If \(y\le23\), this lies in \([189,211]\), a contradiction. Thus every term of \(B\) is at least \(24\). But terms from \(\{24,25\}\) cannot sum to \(187\): seven sum to at most \(175\), while eight sum to at least \(192\).

Now suppose \(s=188\). Every outside term is at least \(24\). If an outside term were \(24\), replacing any \(y\in B\) by it would give \(212-y\); hence every \(y\in B\) would have to be at least \(24\), again impossible because terms from \(\{24,25\}\) cannot sum to \(188\). Therefore every outside term equals \(25\).

Using an outside \(25\), replacing \(y\in B\) gives sum \(213-y\). For every \(2\le y\le24\), this belongs to \([189,211]\). Therefore every term of \(B\), and consequently every term of the whole list, is either \(1\) or \(25\).

Let \(p\) be the number of \(25\)'s. If \(p\ge8\), eight of them sum to \(200\). If \(p\le7\), the total-sum condition guarantees at least \(200-25p\) copies of \(1\); selecting all \(p\) copies of \(25\) and \(200-25p\) copies of \(1\) again gives sum \(200\). Both cases contradict the assumed gap.

Thus every permitted list has a selectable sum in \([189,211]\), so \(N=11\) suffices. Combined with the construction, the minimum is \(11\).
